_readme: Corporate guard pack. ON by default. With git_remote_hosts empty, every push to a remote host is refused until you add your company's git hosts (for example a GitHub Enterprise host). The workbench guard refuses agent edits it can recognise, but it cannot see every program that writes files, so keep permission prompts on. Edit it by hand or re-run the installer with --git-hosts. Keys are documented in plugins/workbench-core/scripts/guards/rulepacks/corporate.py. Publishing and sharing (npm/pnpm/yarn publish, twine, cargo, docker push, scp/rsync/sftp to a remote host, S3/Azure/GCS uploads, gists, releases, PR approvals, admin merges and comments) always asks you first; a copy to a host or bucket listed in upload_hosts is not asked about.
_known_limits: The guard reads the commands Claude runs in the shell. It cannot see commands run from inside a program or script (for example Python or Node), so it catches mistakes, not a determined attempt. Your permission settings and your organisation's own controls (for example repository and network policy) are the real boundary.
